text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- President Le Duc Anh has thanked the Asian Development Bank for its financial assistance for Vietnam since 1993, saying it had been responsible for the execution of many significant development projects.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's People's Committee has approved in principle a proposal for a $115 million tunnel under the Saigon River.
-- Smuggling and trade fraud levels increased in April and early May, according to the General Department of Customs.
-- Ho Chi Minh City has approved a preliminary list of 52 nominees to take part in National Assembly elections in July.
-- Communist Party's General Secretary Do Muoi received a Cuban military delegation on Monday.
-- The State Bank will auction 50 billion ($4.28 million) worth one-year Treasury notes on Wednesday.
-- Vietnam and Italy have signed agreements for a $60 million preferantial loan to Vietnam and implementation of a cultural accord.

-- State legislative, executive, justice, research, training bodies and national data centres will not be allowed to use the Internet, according to a decision issued by the Ministry of Culture and Information.
-- Some 846,500 secondary school pupils will sit final examinations starting on Wednesday.
